body:
PR #1982 for TASK-1297 — the fix for the bug that cost us today's throughput, with one declared scope gap I want you to rule on

Third fanout PR, +538/-11, open and not merged. Same handover as #1977: I wrote the prompt, so I am not forming a verdict.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF rather than taking from the report:
- `EventKind::QueueDrained` gains `excluded_from_batch: usize` carrying `#[serde(default)]`, so old event lines still parse. Same on the drain-state struct. Backward compatibility is real, not asserted.
- The count is derived through the same role-routed queue read that `resolve_batch_members_with_context` uses — `queue_list_with_role_fallback` plus `entry_matches_role_filter` — which is what you asked for, so the figure stays correct under BUG-1264's alias fallback rather than being a second independent walk that can disagree.
- Reported and not re-run by me: 5096 tests pass, fmt clean. The pre-commit hook again caught trace markers in `///` doc comments and they were demoted to plain `//`. That is the third lane in a row to hit that hook, which is the substrate-as-bouncer working exactly as intended — none of those would have been caught by review.

THE SCOPE GAP, AND IT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The single-batch path (`--batch NAME`) is fully wired: start-up line, live drain status, closing summary, and the event. The chained path (`--batch a,b,c`) gets the live `aida drain status` figure but NOT the closing-summary or event figure. It is called out in a code comment as a follow-up rather than silently dropped, which I would rather have than a quiet half-implementation.

My read is that this is acceptable and the follow-up should be filed — the incident shape was the single-batch path, that is what starved sixteen specs today, and the chained path is rarer. But it is your call whether a partially-wired report is worse than none on that path, because a drain that reports the figure live and then omits it from the permanent record is a small instance of the PRIN-4 class: the burndown record would disagree with what the operator saw while it ran.

WORTH NOTING FOR THE LOOP. This spec exists because a stale `--batch` filter hid sixteen approved specs for hours while every wave reported healthy. If it merges, that failure becomes self-reporting: the drain would have said "3 members, 16 other approved specs routed to this role are not in this batch" at start-up and I would have caught it in minutes rather than after the operator asked why the number was not moving.

FANOUT SCORECARD, since you may want it for the seat-handoff work. Five lanes dispatched: BUG-1283 delivered #1977 in 8 minutes, BUG-1285 stalled 19 minutes on the headless-waiting trap and recovered with one resume message to deliver #1980, TASK-1297 delivered #1982 in 45 minutes, and TASK-1292 and BUG-1290 are running with both fixes in the prompt. The drain was unaffected throughout — it kept advancing and produced #1978 and #1981 in parallel. One defect in five, caused by a rule the drain's own prompts carry and mine did not.
